 View Comments A wintry system will enter New England Thursday and linger through Saturday morning. Boston Globe Snow, rain, and blustery winds. An approaching storm system will have it all, with the Boston area seeing all rain while more inland areas and higher elevations will get a first taste of wintry weather in the form of snow. 
 This storm won’t be a potent system, but it will be cold enough in spots to generate as much as 3 to 6 inches of snow across Northern New England as it slides off the Mid-Atlantic coast and develops into a nor’easter . 
 As far as Massachusetts goes? Expect rain east of I-495 and south of the Mass Pike. A changeover to wet snow is expected west of I-495, along Route 2, with a coating to a couple of inches accumulating across Northern Worcester County and into the Berkshires. 
 It’ll also be brisk out there, especially all day Friday (in the 40s) and Saturday morning (the 30s) with the gusty winds, but it just won’t be that cold around Southern New England for widespread snow. Greater Boston may end up with about an inch of cold, windswept rain, not a washout like what we saw last week in Southeastern Mass. 
 Storm timeline
 • Thursday morning/afternoon — Light snow and rain hit Western Massachusetts and parts of Western Vermont Thursday morning. Rain will extend into Greater Boston, Southeastern Mass., Cape Cod, and Rhode Island around the evening commute. 
 • Thursday night/Friday — Scattered pockets of precipitation will continue through Thursday night and much of Friday. Snow will continue across Northern New England and the Northern Berkshires, while cold rain showers will continue across Greater Boston and most of Southern New England. 
 Northern New England and the higher elevations across Massachusetts will begin to see a changeover to a wintry mix as we head into Thursday night and temperatures fall — eventually changing over to all snow overnight into Friday. 
 • Saturday morning — Scattered light rain and snow showers will taper off in the morning. 
 The storm progresses into New England throughout Thursday and lingers through much of Friday. Boston Globe The forecast snowfall totals for our late-week storm-turned-nor'easter. Boston Globe These extra maps below detail the forecast weather elements. 
 The rain-snow line hugs the higher elevations across Interior New England. Boston Globe Forecast rain totals should remain modest for this week's storm, reaching up to an inch at most. Boston Globe Winter weather advisories are in place for portions of Vermont Thursday through Friday morning. Boston Globe Precipitation arrives to Western and Northern New England by mid to late Thursday morning. Boston Globe Thursday will see a coastal storm push into New England, producing some wet snow at times across Western Mass. and Northern New England. Boston Globe Wind gusts should reach 20 to 30 mph across Coastal New England, including Boston, Thursday afternoon through Friday. Boston Globe Highs on Thursday will reach the upper 40s to low 50s across Greater Boston. Boston Globe As of now, the best chance for accumulating snow sits across the interior late in the week. Boston Globe Highs on Thursday across Southern New England. Boston Globe Temperatures Friday morning should sink into the 30s across much of Massachusetts Boston Globe It's going to feel cold on Friday morning with wind chills below freezing in Boston. Boston Globe Highs on Friday should only reach the 30s in some spots of Southern New England. Boston Globe Temperatuers will be coldest Friday night into early Saturday. Boston Globe Wind chills will once again be below freezing across Greater Boston on Saturday morning. Boston Globe Highs on Saturday should return to the 40s across all of Southern New England.
